elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 7.7 reads: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." The prior 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week liquidated damages charge is deleted, and the replacement is unconditional and Agreement-wide, leaving no retained formula, instalment or contingent payment mechanic (the only other payment provision, § 7.3, merely restricts Vendor from charging interest on amounts not due).

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind survives (§ 7.7 now bars all liquidated damages and penalties against Customer), so the condition of this element does not arise.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the Agreement contains no early-termination fee or minimum-fee-on-termination mechanic payable by Customer following the deletion, so no cap is required.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: zero liquidated amounts are payable by Customer under the rendered § 7.7, so there is no competing liquidated charge to displace.

elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Included for completeness — the operative sentence in § 7.7 achieves the stronger preferred outcome, which necessarily satisfies the lesser fallback outcome.

reasons: The preferred checklist is complete: the single element is met by an unconditional, document-wide statement that Customer is not liable for any liquidated damages or penalties, with the offending 15%/week formula fully removed rather than merely narrowed.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to § 7.7, the only Customer-payable liquidated-damages mechanic, and replaces it with one concise sentence. No survival tail, expense language, procedure, extra damages category or unrelated boilerplate was added, and no favourable Customer language (including § 7.3's interest restriction) was deleted.

Intent is preserved: payment timing, invoicing and interest allocation elsewhere are untouched, the deleted sentence is not cross-referenced by any other provision, and the replacement creates no undefined term or dangling reference. Note that the narrow definition of "Fees" (Implementation Fee only) is immaterial here because the redline eliminates rather than recalculates the amount.

No repair needed. The classification as a deviation is correct because the original clause failed the fallback on its material terms (weekly compounding 15% of annual Fees triggered by a ten-day payment delay, not a capped early-termination fee), which also matches the walk-away test for amounts triggered by minor breaches; severity should stay high.
